thread:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: realtime-p99-latency > 3s for service=hosted-inference us-west-2. Threshold breached for 4m. Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat_stream. Pager sent to oncall.
Tim: I'm on it. quick read: p95 jumped from ~450ms to ~1.1s, p99 ~3.2s. spikes coincide with a surge starting 17:42 UTC. Streaming stalls reported by customers. I'm starting live triage. @Ana can you pull tracing? :mag:
Ana: pulling traces now. initial look: increased queueing on runtime-pool-3, high task_wait_time in traces. No obvious code deploys in last 6h. checking autoscaler events.
Alex: looking at infra. autoscaler showed several scale-ups and then some nodes flapping between Ready/NotReady around 17:45. GPU memory pressure on three nodes (gpux-02/03/07) and OOMs noted for lm-worker processes. Could be model cache churn.
Tim: past hour requests per second increased ~2.7x for chat_stream route. Might be a burst from a partner integration. @Jen can you search support tickets for correlated customer reports?
Jen: one support thread from client 'EduAI' reporting repeated stalls starting ~17:46. They attached a snippet: "stream reset after 45s". I'll flag high-priority and create incident customer impact note.
Marcus: PromQL for p99 (prod):
```
quantile_over_time(0.99, histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)))
```
query shows p99 spike aligned with 17:42..17:50 window. Also backend latency broken down by stage shows kv-cache-miss rate up ~3x.
Ana: traces show many cold-kv-cache misses on large-context models. Prefix caching eviction increased at same time. Possibly cache thrash + model reloads causing stalls in streaming path.
Alex: root cause theory: sudden traffic surge + autoscaler churned nodes -> a subset of requests hit nodes with uncached KV, causing long startup token generation and stall for streaming sessions. Also observed liveliness probes failing during high GPU memory pressure.
Tim: mitigation plan: short-term
- Route streaming traffic to model-variant with smaller context (model-x-small) to reduce cache pressure (traffic split config)
- Temporarily increase pool size for runtime-pool-3 by +2 to reduce queueing
- Mark gpux-02/03/07 for drain and reprovision if they keep flapping
- Enable graceful fallback for streaming to non-streaming endpoint for affected clients if stall > 20s
Can someone run the routing change and bump pool now? I'll coordinate.
Alex: applying pool bump and routing change. command:
```
redwood-cli routes update --route /v1/chat_stream --split "80:model-large,20:model-x-small" --env prod --region us-west-2
redwood-cli runtime scale --pool runtime-pool-3 --delta 2
```
Alex: pool scaled +2. route updated to 20% fallback. monitoring.
Tim: watching dashboards. p95 improving to ~700ms, p99 trending down from 3.2s to 1.6s in next 3m. streaming stalls reduced but still seeing a tail at ~18s for some sessions.
Ana: started collecting heap and nvml dumps from flapping nodes for offline analysis. Marked nodes drained. k8s events show kubelet restarts due to OOMKills on lm-worker.
Jen: customer communication: posted to affected customers with incident summary, mitigation steps, and ETA to next update. EduAI acknowledged and asked for timeline.
Marcus: started a short-term alert suppression for noisy autoscaler flaps to avoid paging during mitigation (suppression window 10m). Not suppressing SLO alarms.
Tim: good. escalation: schedule a quick huddle if p99 doesn't drop below 1s within 10m. Also tagging eng-runtime for postmortem. @Alex @Ana please collect artifacts: traces, dumps, autoscaler logs.
Alex: artifacts collected: /artifacts/2140005678/{traces.tar.gz, nvml-dumps.tar.gz, kube-events.log}
Ana: initial root cause hypothesis: cache thrash + autoscaler instability causing node-level OOM -> streaming stalls. Need follow-up: adjust cache eviction policy, model pinning, and autoscaler backoff tuning.
Tim: handing off to eng-runtime for deep dive. I'll keep this thread as incident record. Next update in 30m or earlier if status changes. :thumbsup:
IncidentBot: Incident annotated: severity=SEV2, pager_state=acknowledged, owner=Tim, incident_id=INC-2140005678.
Tim: closing live mitigation window. final interim status: p99 ~900ms, streaming error rate down 85%. Customers notified. Will open postmortem ticket and link artifacts. Thanks team."
